correctness.rationale: Reconstructed X(X-h)=h, a=1-b and the exact (N+1)-order characteristic polynomial. For all N used the modulus equality argument to exclude closed-disk exterior roots. Analytic IFT near odd π branches gives the coefficient -aπ²/(2b²) in N³ log modulus. Proved the maximizing root’s phase is O(1/N), reduced its branch index to a finite set, and compared leading (2m+1)² constants to prove uniqueness. Symbolic coefficient checks and 55-digit direct polynomial residuals at N=100,300,1000 for two h values passed. Numeric checks are diagnostics, not substitutes for the infinite-N argument.

originality.rationale: The 2024 primary arXiv studies and the 2025 related arXiv paper were read in relevant full-text sections for the population model. They establish delay-independent global stability conditions or low-delay local thresholds, not the sharp cubic large-delay spectral gap and unique leading pair. Multiple actual published-finding corpus searches and this ledger’s recoverable claim texts were checked: nearest delayed-cohort and delayed-ring entries do not imply the theorem, and the own Ricker item concerns different undelayed population dynamics. The continuous-time large-delay spectrum literature is broader in spirit but not an identified theorem for this discrete polynomial. Priority remains conditional on unindexed earlier discrete spectral work.
residual_risks: General large-delay *discrete* spectral asymptotics could already imply this special case despite absent indexed search hits.

value.rationale: Recruitment lag naturally modulates delayed populations. The source work proves or plots which regimes are stable but does not quantify the slow high-lag transient exactly at its limiting critical parameter. An explicit N³ relaxation clock with unique oscillatory leading mode is an interpretable sharp dynamical invariant, not a restatement of a finite-dimensional Schur criterion or an arbitrary numerical slice. It explains why arbitrarily long yet finite delays remain locally stable while the approach to equilibrium becomes dramatically slower.
